key_insight: The paper shows that hybrid attention quality depends not just on which layers keep full attention, but on how those layers work together across the network. By modeling layer interdependence, it aims to choose a better full-attention subset for long-context efficiency without sacrificing too much performance.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of converting standard Transformers into efficient hybrid attention models for long-context tasks. Existing layer-selection heuristics often ignore interactions between layers, which can lead to suboptimal hybrid architectures.
method: Analyzes Transformer-to-hybrid conversion by considering dependencies among layers, rather than scoring each layer independently.
Selects a subset of layers to preserve full attention while replacing the remaining layers with linear attention for efficiency.
Seeks a better balance between long-context performance and computational cost than fixed-pattern or heuristic selection strategies.
impact: This matters for practitioners building efficient LLMs and long-context models because it can reduce inference cost while preserving stronger accuracy than naive hybridization. It provides a more principled way to design hybrid attention architectures for real deployment.
